newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends down in cautious trading.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends down in cautious trading.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed down on Thursday, with sentiment remaining cautious amid news of fresh riots in central Java, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index fell 2.67 points, or 0.42 percent, to close at 635.56 points. Decliners led advancers by 65 to 47 with 65 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was 389 billion rupiah. The market was closed on Wednesday due to a public holiday.
"How many more riots to go?" one broker said, adding that there was unlikely to be any rebound before the May 29 general election if the violence continued.

Rioting by supporters of rival political parties erupted again on Java island on Wednesday, and homes, offices and vehicles were damaged in at least two towns including Wonosobo, 350 km (215 miles) east of Jakarta, and Wonosobo's neighbouring town of Banjarnegara, police and a newspaper said on Thursday.

Outbreaks of riots could pick up in the lead-up to the May general election, and although so far this has done little to rock the market, investors are likely to react differently if any riots take place in the capital city, Jos Parengkuan, research director of PT Lippo Securities, said.
The most actively traded Bank BNI rose 25 rupiah to close at 1,375 rupiah following recent falls.

"Bank BNI has relatively strong fundamentals. It was traded at 1,775 rupiah in mid-February but has fallen to the current levels because of weak market sentiment. I recommend a buy at this price," one banking analyst said.
Bank Pikko fell 50 rupiah to 3,950 rupiah after resuming trading in the afternoon session.
The Jakarta stock exchange suspended trading of Bank Pikko late on Tuesday following a 207.69 percent rise in the stock, an exchange official said.
Brokers, however, said the stock exchange's move was far too late, as it should have taken the decision when Pikko rose above 50 percent.
Bank Panin and Bank PDFCI announced rises in their 1996 net profits on Thursday, but it had no impact on their prices, brokers said.
Panin was not traded, while PDFCI was unchanged at 2,325 rupiah in thin trading.
Indonesia's parliament approved five tax bills on Thursday aimed at strengthening state and provincial revenues, the government said.
The announcement did not have much impact on the market, but analysts said they were waiting for more details on the bills and how they could impact companies' earnings.
Inco attracted market attention as it rose 700 rupiah to close at 3,800 rupiah after touching a day high of 4,500 rupiah.
Inco said earlier that the firm planned to buy back about 20 percent of its stock, a newspaper reported.
Matahari was traded at 3,300 rupiah at the cross board with some 10 million shares traded, but details were not clear, brokers said. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
